dedupe_keys.name: 2017 atlantic hurricane season impact on communications fcc report hurricane maria in puerto rico

description: This post-event analysis by the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau of the US Federal Communications Commission (PS Docket No. 17-344, August 2018) reports how Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Nate and above all Maria affected wireless, wireline, cable and broadcast communications in 2017, what the Commission did in response, and what it recommends. Using Disaster Information Reporting System (DIRS) data, it shows that Harvey's effects on wireless service in Texas were largely remedied within a week, whereas after Maria up to 95.6 percent of cell sites in Puerto Rico and 76.6 percent in the US Virgin Islands were out of service, 48 of Puerto Rico's 78 municipios had every cell site down, and six months later 4.3 and 12 percent of sites were still out. It records the Commission's special temporary authorities, public notices, orders and experimental licences such as Project Loon, summarises comments from carriers and public-safety bodies, and recommends best practices on backup power, coordination, the Wireless Resiliency Cooperative Framework and restoration. Coverage: Texas, Florida, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands, by county or municipio and day. Format and access: free PDF and text on docs.fcc.gov, a US government work. Caveats: DIRS reporting is voluntary and was deactivated in places; carriers' figures are self-reported. Simulation uses: hazard exposure and recovery curves of communication networks under hurricanes, cascading dependence on power, emergency response and restoration planning. Related records: FCC DIRS is the underlying data source, and a GAO review (GAO-21-297) assessed the FCC's Maria response.
